_comment: SHA-256 of rl-engine/core at the Phase D boundary (after documented gap fixes GAP-1 and GAP-2, before/without any domain-specific edits). Regenerate only when a platform-level gap fix is made and record it in documentedGaps.

documentedGaps.title: Action-space addressing was incomplete (spec §5)
documentedGaps.rationale: The DSL declared five action-space kinds, but continuous and multiDiscrete had no type discriminator and validateAction only checked type membership — neither kind was addressable or validatable at runtime. Necessary platform abstraction: a type field per kind and a single validateActionAgainstSpace covering all five kinds, shared by the runtime step pipeline and the compiler.

documentedGaps.title: Effect values were literals only (spec §31 subset)
documentedGaps.rationale: Rules could not express state-dependent magnitudes (e.g. cash -= shares × price in any trading domain; proportional transfers in logistics). Implemented the spec §31 controlled-function subset — declarative $field/$mul/$add/$sub/$div resolution, sandboxed, no eval — as a platform primitive in applyEffect.

documentedGaps.title: The PRNG internal state was inaccessible — mid-episode checkpointing impossible (spec §29/§45)
documentedGaps.rationale: Restoring a snapshot into a fresh process requires resuming the mulberry32 stream exactly; the internal state (a single integer) was private to the closure, so any restore would restart the sequence and diverge from an uninterrupted run. Necessary platform abstraction: snapshotState()/restoreState() on the draw function + RandomService, and optional snapshot()/restore() on the Environment interface. This is the last piece §29 checkpoint-restore needs.

documentedGaps.title: The §34-35 Trainer seam was unusable and the ReplayBuffer was nondeterministic (rl/ layer, outside the hash-checked core set — ledgered here for completeness)
documentedGaps.rationale: Trainer.train(policy, episodes) gave a trainer NO environment access, so §34's Trainer-orchestrates-Environment-Policy diagram was unrealizable; the seam now receives an environment factory + episode context. ReplayBuffer.sample() used Math.random, violating the §28 determinism rule; sampling now flows through the seeded RandomService with serializable RNG state. The algorithm remains entirely in the trainer implementation — the core engine is untouched by Phase F.

documentedGaps.title: Declarative effect values were rejected by the set-type pre-flight (red team R2)
documentedGaps.rationale: The state_compatibility layer validated effect.value against the state schema BEFORE resolving {$field}/{$mul}/{$add}/{$sub}/{$div} descriptors, so any set with a declarative reference failed with e.g. 'set rejected: filing_day: expected integer'. The $-resolution platform primitive (GAP-2) was therefore unusable in set effects at runtime — a legal domain-pack workflow (legal-filing file_motion_rule) could never fire. Fix: resolve the descriptor via resolveEffectValue first, validate the RESOLVED value; unresolvable references remain runtime no-ops per applyEffect semantics. Found by the authorized red team engagement (RedTeamTest/REDTEAM_REPORT.md R2).
